unit.title: Shapes, Area and Volume
unit.blurb: Converting area units, hectares, the area of a triangle, and the volume and surface area of cubes and cuboids.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Convert between area units: mm², cm² and m².

O2.t: Know that 1 hectare = 10 000 m² and convert between hectares and square metres.

O3.t: Use the formula area = ½ × base × height for triangles.

O4.t: Calculate the volume of cubes and cuboids.

O5.t: Calculate the surface area of cubes and cuboids from their nets.

p: A shop sells floor tiles priced **per square metre**, but your floor plan is in **square centimetres**: the floor is **180 000 cm²**.
How many square metres is that? (Hint: it is NOT 1800.) Try it before you read on.
A square 1 m by 1 m is also 100 cm by 100 cm. Its area is **1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm²**.
p2: You multiply by the length factor **twice**, because area has two dimensions.

p: Bigger unit → smaller unit: **multiply** (the number gets bigger). Smaller unit → bigger unit: **divide**.
Or convert the lengths first: a 2.5 m × 40 cm rug = 250 cm × 40 cm = 10 000 cm² = 1 m².

lesson.t: How do I convert area units?
p: Step 1: Write the length conversion (e.g. 1 m = 100 cm).
Step 2: Square it for area (1 m² = 10 000 cm²).
Step 3: Bigger → smaller unit: multiply. Smaller → bigger: divide.
Step 4: Check the size makes sense; or convert the lengths before working out the area.

p: Any triangle fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height, and it takes up exactly **half** of it.

head: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height
A = ½bh

p2: The **height** is the **perpendicular** height: it meets the base (or the base extended) at a right angle. The slanted side is NOT the height.

p: Any side can be the base, as long as you use the height perpendicular to it.
p2: For an obtuse triangle, the height may fall outside the triangle (on the base extended). Here base 6 cm, height 4 cm: A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 cm².

Step 2: Find the perpendicular height to that base (it makes a right angle).
Step 3: Area = ½ × base × height; units are squared.
Step 4: Ignore slanted sides that are not the height.

sections.title: Calculating the volume of cubes and cuboids

p: A delivery box is **30 cm long, 20 cm wide and 10 cm high**. You want to fill it with **1 cm sugar cubes**.
How many sugar cubes fit? Try it before you read on.
30 cm × 20 cm = 600 cm².

qq.prompt: A rectangle is 12 cm by 5 cm. Area?

p: **Volume** is the amount of space a 3D shape takes up, measured in **cubic units**: cm³, m³, mm³.
One layer of the box: 30 × 20 = 600 cubes. There are 10 layers: 600 × 10 = **6000 cubes**.
**Capacity** is how much a container holds. **1 cm³ = 1 ml** and **1000 cm³ = 1 litre**.
The box (6000 cm³) would hold **6 litres** of water if it were waterproof.
A cube of side 4 cm: V = 4³ = 64 cm³.

qq.prompt: A cuboid is 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm. Volume (cm³)?

lesson.t: How do I find the volume of a cuboid?
p: Step 1: Check all three lengths are in the same units.
Step 2: Multiply length × width × height (any order).
Step 3: Give the answer in cubic units (cm³, m³).
Step 4: For capacity, use 1000 cm³ = 1 litre.
